ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of each director, shareholder, UBO, and related party against the New Zealand Sanctions Act 2019 list, the New Zealand Police Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) PEP database, the United Nations Consolidated Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List, EU/UK consolidated sanctions lists, and commercial third-party screening tools (e.g., World-Check, Dow Jones). The protocol requires enhanced due diligence (EDD) for any PEP, including senior management approval, source-of-wealth documentation, and continuous transaction monitoring. Negative news and adverse media checks are mandatory. All screening results are documented and retained for a minimum of 5 years under the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office – Companies Register (online portal at https://app.companiesoffice.govt.nz/companies-register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in the Latin alphabet (English or Te Reo Māori); non-Latin scripts are not accepted. Names must consist of letters, numbers, spaces, and permitted punctuation (typically only ampersand, apostrophe, plus sign, full stop, comma, hyphen, and parentheses), and must end with 'Limited', 'Tapui (Limited)' or the approved abbreviation 'Ltd'. The name must not be identical or almost identical to an existing name on the Names Index and must not be likely to mislead. Where a foreign-language name is desired, the applicant must provide a romanised/English transliteration, and the registered name must appear in English/Māori script on the public register.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a proposed name is rejected, the incorporation agent may immediately file a new name reservation application with a more distinctive element, or apply to the Registrar for a reconsideration under section 23(3) of the Companies Act 1993 on the grounds that the name passes the 'not likely to mislead' test. For rejected names containing restricted or sensitive words, prior written consent from the relevant Minister, statutory body, or approval authority must be obtained and submitted with the name reservation. Where the Registrar issues a formal refusal, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court of New Zealand, with application to be made within 20 working days of the refusal date. If the initial reservation expires, a new reservation may be requested for an additional 20 working-day period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted, with conditions. The registered office must be a physical New Zealand street address (a PO Box is prohibited) at which documents can be served and the company registers are kept. A virtual office/serviced office in Auckland, Wellington, or Christchurch that provides a physical street address and forwarding services is accepted by the New Zealand Companies Office. There is no statutory requirement for a physical server, operational headquarters, or employees to be located in New Zealand for a VPN/software company. The arrangement must include a registered agent with a New Zealand address for service of process; non-resident directors are generally allowed but may trigger a requirement for a New Zealand resident agent or director depending on the structure.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-Moderate quantified risk: approximately 10% annual probability of an unannounced site inspection or AML/CFT field audit by the New Zealand Police, Department of Internal Affairs, or the Companies Office during the first full year of operation. For a medium-risk VPN/SaaS entity with international payment rails, the probability may rise to 15% if the company handles crypto-asset payments, cross-border payroll, or other enhanced-risk indicators. The Companies Office typically conducts paper-only compliance reviews, but the AML/CFT supervision authorities may conduct on-site inspections without notice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.commercial_substance_expectations: The company will be expected to maintain up-to-date company registers, a registered office of substance in New Zealand, and an active corporate services/registered agent relationship. For tax-exempt status under the International Company classification (as applied), the entity must comply with non-resident ownership and business activity restrictions, and must not derive domestic New Zealand source income.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, especially ss 10–24 (incorporation), s 30 (constitution), ss 35–41 (company name), ss 122–127 (board governance), s 153 (director duties), s 191 (registered office), s 222 (share register), and the Companies (Forms) Regulations 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form NZINZ – Application for Registration of a Company (Company Incorporation Application) lodged electronically with the New Zealand Companies Office
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 1993, and no escrow or bank deposit is required. The company may allot fully paid or partly paid shares; the constitution and incorporation application will state the initial subscribed capital, typically 100 ordinary shares at NZ$1.00 each.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporation application and the subscription contract attached to the application are provisionally adopted, and the subscribers' acceptance of allotment of 100 fully paid ordinary shares of NZ$1.00 each, in accordance with the constitution, is confirmed, with such shares to be entered in the company's share register upon issue. RESOLVED that the registered office of the company shall be established at the physical New Zealand address set forth in the incorporation application, and that the directors are authorized to file Form COO with the New Zealand Companies Office and to maintain a register of addresses. RESOLVED that [Name Surname] is appointed sole director and chairperson; [Name Surname] is appointed company secretary; and [Name Surname] is appointed compliance officer, each to act until removed or replaced by ordinary resolution or in accordance with the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED FURTHER that the appointed officers are severally authorized to execute the banking mandate, lease agreements, and all contracts reasonably necessary for the initial business, subject to the company's constitution and applicable law. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online register (www.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search against the Companies Register and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) database. File an electronic name reservation application if the proposed name passes the section 20 screening criteria of the Companies Act 1993. The registrar rejects names that are identical or confusingly similar to an existing entity or that may be prohibited under the Companies (Trading Names) Regulations 2014.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and secondary names
Statement explaining the use of any restricted word or phrase, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is queried or refused, submit a revised name reservation using a more distinctive suffix or a materially different composite name. A refusal may be challenged by written representation to the Registrar; if still unresolved, the prospective incorporator may seek judicial review in the High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Constitution and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and proposed directors under the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft a company constitution compliant with s 30 of the Companies Act 1993, covering share rights, director appointment and removal, board quorums, shareholder meetings, indemnities, and dispute resolution. Obtain signed consents from all initial directors and shareholders. Confirm registered office and address for service in New Zealand. Where non-resident directors are appointed, ensure at least one director satisfies the New Zealand/Australian residence requirement in s 155(2) unless an applicable exemption is obtained.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as a director
Consent to act as a shareholder
Notice of registered office and address for service
Full legal names, dates of birth, residential addresses, and occupations of all directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar considers that a constitutional provision is invalid or conflicts with the Companies Act 1993, the board must adopt an amending special resolution and resubmit the constitution. Inconsistencies with statutory provisions may be cured by deletion of the offending clause and by reaffirming the default statutory regime.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgement of the Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office online incorporation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the Companies Office portal using a verified RealMe account. Complete Form NZINZ electronically, attach the constitution, director and shareholder consents, registered office details, and the reserve name reference where applicable. Verify all data against identity documents, pay the application fee by card or direct debit, and submit the application. The application must contain the statutory declaration or electronic equivalent confirming compliance with ss 12–17 of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Consent to act forms for each director and shareholder
Registered office and address for service details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a notice of defect under s 14, the applicant has 20 working days to supply corrected information or missing documents. If the defect notice is not cured, the application is deemed abandoned, and the incorporating party may re-lodge a fresh application with the required evidence and pay a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registry Verification and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar verifies the application, name availability, constitution, director consent forms, and payment. Upon approval, the company is registered, allocated a unique company number and NZBN, and issued an electronic Certificate of Incorporation. The legal existence of the company begins on the date and time specified in the certificate under s 14(3) of the Companies Act 1993.
required_dossiers: Company extract confirming the registered office and first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical or typographical error, apply to the Registrar for administrative correction. If incorporation is refused, seek High Court review under s 18 of the Companies Act 1993 on the ground of procedural error or jurisdictional mistake.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting and Initial Corporate Governance Actions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors under the Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting and pass the pro-forma First Board Resolution. Adopt the registered office, approve the share allotment, appoint officers, approve the banking mandate, and resolve that the constitution and governance arrangements are in force. Record all decisions in board minutes and maintain the statutory registers, including the share register, director register, and registered office register.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a statutory declaration or consent is found defective, ratify the affected decision by a further board resolution and file the corrected consent with the Companies Office. Late filing penalties may be remedied by an explanation to the Registrar and, where appropriate, an application for waiver under the Companies (Fees) Regulations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings and Initial Register Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and company officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, issue share certificates, populate all statutory registers, and file any post-incorporation notices required by the Registrar, including confirmation of share allotments and officer details. Register for the annual return cycle and, as applicable, obtain the Inland Revenue number and other registrations necessary for opening bank accounts and engaging employees. Maintain the registered office as a real physical New Zealand address capable of receiving service of process.
required_dossiers: IRD number application and confirmation, if not previously obtained
Company extract showing current directors and registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, file immediately online and request a late-filing penalty waiver or remission. If the company is struck off for failure to file, an application may be made to the Registrar under s 319 of the Companies Act 1993 for restoration of the company name within the applicable limitation period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) and WorkSafe New Zealand; no sector-specific industrial licence is prescribed for an ISIC 6201 VPN and digital encryption software business.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – No industry-specific operating or manufacturing licence applies. The company must nevertheless hold general office-occupancy approvals required by the Building Act 2004 and fire safety legislation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – No Environmental Impact Assessment is required because the VPN/privacy software activity is an information-technology service conducted in commercial premises and is not an activity listed in Schedule 4 of the Resource Management (National Environmental Standards) Regulations 2016.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater, VOC, or combustion emissions are generated by normal software operations. Office wastewater discharge must comply with the local district council trade-waste by-laws; electronic waste must be disposed through a licensed recycler under the Waste Minimisation Act 2008; any backup-battery or electrical equipment disposal must conform to the Hazardous Substances (Hazardous Waste) Regulations 2017.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The office premises must obtain a building code compliance certificate and, where applicable, a Building Warrant of Fitness under the Building Act 2004. A fire evacuation scheme must be approved by Fire and Emergency New Zealand under the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017. Workplace safety duties, accident registers, and electrical installation inspections must be completed in accordance with WorkSafe New Zealand requirements under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and the Electricity (Safety) Regulations 2010.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake) of New Zealand; online portal: myIR at https://www.ird.govt.nz
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity obtains a New Zealand IRD number as a non-resident company by submitting Form IR742 (Application for Registration by a Non-Resident Company) to Inland Revenue, together with a certified certificate of incorporation and any required constitutional documents from the home jurisdiction. Following IRD number allocation, the entity may separately apply for GST registration via myIR using Form GST101A (Registration of Non-Resident Company) once the relevant New Zealand GST nexus threshold is met. The International Company (CK_IC) structure is treated as a non-resident company and may obtain a dedicated IRD number without maintaining a physical New Zealand registered office or resident director for tax registration purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone / Non-Resident Territorial Scope: The International Company is treated as outside the New Zealand full tax net; only New Zealand-sourced income is assessable, while foreign-sourced income remains exempt. No pass-through eligibility exists; the entity is taxed at entity level on New Zealand-sourced income only, with non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) or approved issuer levy applying to certain outbound payments, and the entity is not subject to New Zealand income tax on offshore business income derived from VPN/digital services sold to non-resident customers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not offer a check-the-box or elective entity-classification regime comparable to the US. The default statutory classification of a company is a separate taxable entity. Available mechanisms include: (i) voluntary GST registration for non-resident suppliers of remote services even below the NZD 60,000 threshold in order to claim input tax credits; (ii) the remote-services registration mode under section 54B of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, which allows non-resident digital suppliers to GST-register solely for NZ-resident consumer supplies; (iii) hybrid mismatch adjustment elections under sections FH 1 to FH 14 of the Income Tax Act 2007 to neutralise double non-taxation outcomes; and (iv) the approved issuer levy election (2% instead of NRWT on offshore interest) for New Zealand-sourced interest paid to non-resident investors.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value added tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies made in New Zealand over any 12-month period; for non-resident suppliers of remote services (including VPN and digital privacy applications), the same NZD 60,000 threshold applies based on supplies made to New Zealand-resident consumers. Voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or government API transaction-screening mandate. E-invoicing is voluntary and operates on the Peppol interoperability framework with UBL 2.1/Peppol BIS 3.0 standards via accredited Access Points. GST returns are filed periodically through myIR (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly) and must be accompanied by a digital GST return data transmission; documentary retention obligations apply under section 51 of the GST Act 1985. No fiscal seal or real-time tax authority pre-approval of invoices exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to (i) goods physically exported from New Zealand within 28 days of supply (or within 60 days for hire-purchase or conditional sale supplies); (ii) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed (section 11A, GST Act 1985); and (iii) remote or digital services, including VPN network privacy applications, supplied to a non-resident recipient where the recipient is not in New Zealand at the time of supply. The supplier must hold reasonable documentary evidence of the recipient's non-resident status, such as geolocation/IP data, registered business address, non-resident payment gateway country codes, or contractual declarations. Supplies of digital services to New Zealand-resident consumers are reverse situations and remain taxable at 15% GST under the remote-services regime.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CUSDEC) lodged electronically in the Trade Single Window (TSW) for physical goods exports
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical export movement out of New Zealand
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or equivalent bank statement evidencing foreign currency settlement from the overseas customer
Commercial invoice and purchase order describing the digital nature of the VPN/privacy software service and confirming the non-resident status of the buyer for services supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue may retrospectively claw back zero-rated GST where the exporter fails to substantiate timely export, non-resident supply, or foreign currency repatriation within the evidenced timeframe. Misdeclaration triggers reassessments, GST shortfall penalties under Schedule 1 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 (up to 20% for lack of reasonable care, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or fraudulent intent), plus use-of-money interest under sections 120–124 of the TAA 1994. The reassessment period is generally four years, extended to seven years for fraudulent or knowingly incorrect GST returns. Knowingly providing false export documentation may constitute an offence under section 143B of the TAA 1994, carrying criminal penalties including imprisonment. All zero-rating substantiation records must be retained for at least seven years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Putea Matua), established under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989; for the Cook Islands International Company (CK_IC), the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission performs financial-services licensing and AML/CFT supervision, while monetary and currency operations remain anchored to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand through New Zealand-dollar circulation and New Zealand-dollar clearing arrangements.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains a fully liberalized foreign-exchange and capital-control regime. There are no exchange controls restricting current-account or capital-account convertibility, and no Reserve Bank approval is required for inbound capital injections, profit remittances, dividend distributions, royalty payments, or liquidation proceeds. Both residents and non-residents may freely transact in New Zealand dollars (NZD) and foreign currencies. The New Zealand dollar is a freely floating and freely convertible currency. The only relevant statutory gateways are sector-specific foreign-investment screening under the Overseas Investment Act 2005 for sensitive land and significant business assets, and general AML/CFT obligations under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. For the tax-exempt CK_IC vehicle, profit repatriation and capital return are not subject to exchange-control permission, but must be supported by auditable corporate documentation, beneficial-ownership declarations, and source-of-funds evidence retained by the paying bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio apply to export receipts in New Zealand. Exporters are not obliged to surrender foreign-exchange proceeds to the Reserve Bank of New Zealand or to convert them into NZD within any prescribed period. Export proceeds may be credited directly to a foreign-currency account or an NZD account, and may be held, hedged, or converted at commercial discretion. The only reporting requirement is indirect and statistical: banks and financial institutions report international transactions for balance-of-payments purposes under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's International Transactions Reporting requirements, with no surrender, repatriation, or conversion condition attached.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High, but subject to legal constraints. Offshore digital electronic-money institutions (EMIs) may offer multi-currency virtual accounting and settlement through partner banks, and some UK/EU-established EMIs with New Zealand Financial Service Provider (FSP) registration or a New Zealand AML/CFT reporting entity can provide viable payment rails. However, an offshore EMI cannot independently represent a domestic New Zealand bank account number, cannot perform deposit-taking or lending without New Zealand regulatory authorizations, and must route NZD clearing through an established local banking partner or an NZD-clearing bank. The CK_IC treasury can use such EMIs for low-value operational flows from Stripe and Paymentwall, but should maintain a primary corporate account at a licensed New Zealand commercial bank for high-value capital movements, escrow arrangements, and hedge execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under New Zealand law, directors and beneficial owners are not statutorily required to appear physically in front of a New Zealand bank for account opening. Non-face-to-face identification is permitted if the reporting entity uses reliable and independent electronic identification methods, certified copies of passports, notarized corporate documents, and enhanced due diligence appropriate to the risk profile. In practice, tier-1 banks may apply internal policies requiring at least one natural-person director with a verifiable residential address, introduction by an existing bank relationship, or a local agent for the International Company. A board resolution, current register of directors and shareholders, certificate of incorporation, certificate of good standing, and a documented rationale for the New Zealand banking relationship are mandatory. The physical interview mandate is therefore not absolute: remote onboarding is possible, but a structured remote or video interview will almost always be required by the bank's compliance team.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company lacking visible domestic economic substance or local payroll may be flagged as a shell or conduit risk under the bank's AML/CFT red-flag framework.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the following documentation: certificate of incorporation and good standing for the CK_IC, current register of directors and registered agent, beneficial-ownership declaration, board resolution authorizing account opening, a dated corporate business plan for the VPN/Network-Security SaaS operation, commercial contracts with customers/distributors, invoicing pipeline from Stripe and Paymentwall, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for the shareholders, and bank reference letters from the account-opening jurisdiction where possible.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: VPN and privacy-application revenue may be associated with anonymity-related red flags, cryptocurrency-derived receipts, or cross-border payments routed through payment aggregators, creating enhanced due diligence scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the merchant settlement statements from Stripe and Paymentwall, current product terms of service and acceptable-use policy, sub-processor and data-privacy compliance documentation, evidence that no unlawful anonymity or money-laundering services are marketed, recurring transaction data demonstrating genuine subscription sales, internal transaction monitoring and sanction-screening procedures, and an independent audit or accountant's letter confirming the revenue trail.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity or non-face-to-face KYC may trigger a refusal where ultimate owners hold indirect interests through trusts or offshore structures without a transparent ownership paper trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit notarized/certified passports of all directors and shareholders, proof of residential address for each natural person, registry extracts or trust deeds and deed of trust termination pages showing the full beneficial-ownership chain, independent electronic identity verification results, negative-media check reports, and sworn declarations confirming no politically exposed persons (PEPs) or unexplained wealth.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections for the CK_IC should be routed via SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate parent or beneficial owner to the designated NZD escrow/operational account held at the chosen tier-1 New Zealand bank. The payment message must include a clear purpose code corresponding to 'equity capital injection', 'shareholder loan', or 'other investment capital' under the bank's international transactions reporting framework. The bank will carry out sanction screening, beneficial-ownership verification, and source-of-funds checks; capital may be converted to NZD immediately or held in a foreign-currency account at the bank. No Reserve Bank approval, exchange-control license, or surrender obligation applies. For accounting and audit certainty, retain the executed capital subscription agreement, board resolution, remittance advice, SWIFT confirmation, and bank statement reflecting the credit to the capital escrow account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the VPN/network-privacy SaaS business should be settled using SWIFT MT103 for direct beneficiary wires, or SWIFT MT202 for interbank cover where a beneficiary receives value through a correspondent relationship. For physical network-infrastructure purchases or hardware licensing, a Commercial Letter of Credit is permissible and may be opened through the New Zealand issuing bank using Incoterms-based trade documents; all outbound payments must be accompanied by transaction-specific purpose codes, underlying invoices, merchant settlement reconciliations for SaaS subscriptions, and, where applicable, export or re-export compliance documentation. Stripe and Paymentwall merchant settlement funds can be swept daily into the primary NZD account using pooled payout structures, then allocated to treasury, tax-exempt distributions, or vendor payments only after reconciliation with a compliant audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable spot and forward contracts in NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, and NZD/CNY with a licensed New Zealand trading bank
Outright foreign-exchange forwards and rollover forwards for known subscription and vendor payment cash-flow cycles
Cross-currency swaps between NZD and major convertible currencies for long-term capital-structure hedges
Currency swaps with licensed counterparties to convert non-NZD revenue streams into NZD or the treasury's functional currency
Plain-vanilla foreign-exchange options (buy or sell) transacted under the bank's master derivatives agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are not ordinarily necessary for NZD, as the New Zealand dollar is freely convertible; NDFs may be documented only for exotic emerging-market currency legs when the bank offers a workable pricing and collateral protocol
